title: System Load
hook: Running at 100% capacity feels productive right up until one surprise knocks everything over.
statement: Every system has a breaking point, and overload is what pushes it into collapse.
explainer: When you're maxed out, there's no room for a sick day, a big client ask, or a broken tool. Keeping some buffer is what lets you absorb the hits.
sop: List every client, project, and commitment pulling on you.
Count your Demand and estimate your sustainable Capacity.
Work out your Load Ratio: Demand ÷ Capacity.
If it's above 0.7, cut or delegate one thing this week.
Keep at least 20% of your capacity open for surprises.
equation_example: Demand is 8 active commitments. Capacity is 10. 8 ÷ 10 = 0.8. Above 0.7 means overload, where quality and consistency start slipping. Below 0.7 means you've got buffer to handle shocks.
question: Work out your load ratio right now, and if it's over 0.7, pick one thing to cut.
closing_statement: Leave room, or the next surprise breaks something.
caption:
Principle Nº 130: System Load

Running at 100% capacity feels productive right up until one surprise knocks everything over.

Every system has a breaking point, and overload is what pushes it into collapse.

Your turn: Work out your load ratio right now, and if it's over 0.7, pick one thing to cut.
